THE DIESEL FUEL IMPACTED AN AREA ON THE ASPHALT PARKING LOT APPROXIMATELY 600' X 300'. A STORM DRAIN ON THE PARKING LOT WAS POTENTIALLY IMPACTED BY THE RELEASE. ERTS DISPATCHED EVERGREEN ENVIRONMENTAL TO THE SITE TO PERFORM NECESSARY REMEDIATION ACTIVITIES. EVERGREEN PERSONNEL ARE CURRENTLY ON SITE WITH WEST VIRGINIA DEP REPRESENTATIVE TO PERFORM NECESSARY REMEDIATION ACTIVITIES.

properties.title: NRC Report: Gas Oil: Cracked near Charlotte Courthouse, VA
properties.summary: Incident Type: PIPELINE - NRC Report ID: 938640 - Medium Affected: LAND - Suspected Responsible Party: COLONIAL PIPELINE
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 938640
Incident Time: 2010-03-31 14:00:00
Nearest City: Charlotte Courthouse, VA
Incident Type: PIPELINE
Material: GAS OIL: CRACKED
Medium Affected: LAND
Suspected Responsible Party: COLONIAL PIPELINE
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 46 gallons
ON JANUARY 5TH DURING ROUTINE STATION CHECK, THE SENIOR OPERATOR NOTICED STAINED GRAVEL BETWEEN SUCTION VALVE AND INJECTION VALVES. A WORK CREW WAS CALLED TO INVESTIGATE AND DIG TEST HOLES AROUND APPURTENANCES ASSOCIATED WITH THE PIPELINE TO INVESTIGATE WHETHER OR NOT THE STAINING WAS ASSOCIATED WITH A LEAK. AFTER DIGGING AN INITIAL TEST HOLE TO A DEPTH OF ABOUT 2 TO 3 FT., GROUND WATER BEGAN FILLING THE HOLE AND A SMALL AMOUNT OF BLACK LOOKING OIL BEGAN TO EXUDE INTO THE TEST HOLE. UPON FINDING PRODUCT, THE LOOP WAS ISOLATED FROM THE MAIN LINE BY CLOSING OFF SUCTION AND DISCHARGE VALVES. SORBENT MATERIALS WERE USED TO REMOVE OIL FROM THE WATER SURFACE IN THE TEST HOLE. THE ADDITIONAL TEST HOLES ALSO FILLED WITH GROUND WATER AND SEVERAL EXUDED OIL ON TO THE GROUND WATER SURFACE. OIL WAS ALSO OBSERVED IN THE OIL/WATER SEPARATOR (OWS). TO ENSURE THAT OIL WOULD NOT REACH THE OWS DISCHARGE POINT AT THE POND, THE OWS DISCHARGE VALVE WAS CLOSED AND DISCHARGE WAS ONLY ALLOWED DIRECTLY INTO THE SUMP. MONITORING OF THE OWS AND PRODUCT RECOVERY WAS INITIATED ON A DAILY BASIS.

Report Description
CALLER STATED THAT THEY HAD A NS TRUCK (HIGH RAIL TRUCK) THAT WAS TRAVELING SOUTH BOUND ON THE STATE RT 52 AND ENCOUNTERED A NORTH BOUND VEHICLE (CHEVY AVALANCHE) WHICH CROSSED THE CENTER LINE IN THE PATH OF THE COMPANY VEHICLE IMPACTING HEAD ON. THE COMPANY VEHICLE CAUGHT FIRE AND WAS A TOTAL LOSS. THE AVALANCHE DRIVER WAS NOT RESPONSIVE. A FOLLOWING NS VEHICLE ASSISTED AND PULLED THE AVALANCHE AWAY FROM THE BURNING VEHICLE. THE AVALANCHE DRIVER WAS TRANSPORTED TO THE HOSPITAL AND REPORTS INDICATE A FATALITY. THE RAIL EMPLOYEE SUFFERED MINOR INJURIES AND THEY WERE TRANSPORTED BY PRIVATE VEHICLE TO THE HOSPITAL.
